summary: SSE midstream sequence gap causes cutoff and attachment mismatch (partial base64 embeds)
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports SSE-based streaming sessions frequently cut off mid-attachment when the model returns binary content encoded as base64 (image/png). The client receives partial base64 blocks and a truncated final event; attempting to decode the image fails. This appears only from certain customer networks and correlates with higher connection churn (TLS splice/ALB handoffs).

Impact:
- Several requests to our hosted API return incomplete base64 attachments, causing product features (in-app previews) to fail for the customer.
- Affects enterprise customer Acme Analytics (high usage of embeddings+image-generation flows).

Environment:
- Hosted API (prod us-east) behind ALB -> edge-proxy -> streaming-proxy -> serving-runtime
- Model: redwood/open-13b-v1
- Client: Electron-based desktop app with SSE fallback to long-poll in rare cases

Steps to reproduce (observed by customer):
1) Initiate SSE streaming request that includes an image embed payload (server sends base64 image in a concluding event).
2) Network triggers a short-lived connection splice (customer NAT/edge routing or ALB idle probe).
3) SSE stream resumes but final event is truncated; attachment base64 payload is missing the last few bytes or padded incorrectly.

Observed behavior:
- Final SSE event is missing closing bracket and/or base64 padding characters.
- Client decoder throws invalid-base64 errors.
- Server logs show the session completed and emitted the full payload, but the proxy/handoff trace shows a sequence gap between fragments.

Expected behavior:
- Stream resume should deliver the entire terminal event (complete base64 payload) or trigger deterministic resume/fail policy (explicit EOF marker).

Attachments/logs provided by customer:
- sse_trace_2026-03-09.txt (headers and per-chunk offsets)
- base64_sample_partial.txt (truncated payload)
- client-pcap-0310.zip (network capture around connection splice)
steps_to_reproduce: Create SSE request that streams a base64-encoded image as terminal event
Simulate short connection splice (client IP path migration / ALB idle probe)
Observe that final event delivered to client is truncated and base64 decode fails

comments: 2026-03-10 11:18 Priya Shah (Support): Filed with initial customer artifacts and priority P1. Customer reports ~6% of image attachments fail during heavy churn windows.

2026-03-10 12:05 Miguel Ortega (SRE): Acknowledged. Asking for streaming-proxy and edge-proxy traces. Tentative hypothesis: sequence numbering gap at proxy during socket handoff; may be a hole in the reassembly logic when proxy rebinds to a different upstream connection.

2026-03-10 14:40 Acme Support (Customer): Uploaded PCAP and confirmed failure reproduces when client goes from wifi->cellular quickly (path migration). Also observed when corporate firewall performs TLS-inspection rebinds.

2026-03-11 09:22 Lina Chen (Streaming Eng): Reproduced locally by simulating TCP half-close + splice at the streaming-proxy. Observed missing chunk 543 being dropped by proxy read-loop on fast rebind; serving-runtime retained full event. Preparing patch to ensure in-flight buffers are flushed to downstream before swapping sockets.

2026-03-12 10:01 Miguel Ortega (SRE): Rolled temporary mitigation in edge: increase ALB idle timeout and add spike-detection to avoid immediate reassignment during short probes. Monitoring for regressions.

2026-03-12 16:30 Priya Shah (Support): Notified customer of mitigation and collected a week of telemetry; customer reports success in 98% of cases after mitigation. Leaving open until PR merged and long-term fix deployed.
investigation_notes: PCAP shows 3-way rebind where client issues path migration; sequence numbers in streaming protocol used by proxy incremented, but one fragment never re-emitted to new socket.
streaming-proxy read-loop uses ephemeral ring buffer; on socket swap there was a race where the buffer pointer advanced without copying outstanding fragment to new writer.

Hypothesis: combination of ALB health probe + client NAT rebind results in two quick socket endpoints; proxy attempts fast socket swap and loses a small fragment when application-layer framing crosses the swap boundary.
Temporary mitigation: extend socket quiesce period and enforce flush of pending frames to new writer before drop. Long-term: add robust fragment-id checks and retransmit on gap detection.
Related bug: SUP-314159 describes a different symptom (offset drift) but shares the reassembly codepath; coordinate fixes to avoid regressions.
Confluence note created: SSE fragment reassembly runbook and probe checklist (see related_confluence_pages).
next_steps: Complete streaming-proxy patch to copy pending frames on socket handoff (PR 3421) and add unit tests that simulate path migration
Merge PR and roll to canary edge-proxy cluster in us-east
After canary verification, schedule full rollout and monitor 'attachment_fail_rate' metric for Acme tenant
Update streaming runbook with detection query and mitigation steps
resolution: Mitigation deployed (increased ALB idle timeout + quiesce enforcement). Engineering patch merged to streaming-proxy (PR 3421) and scheduled for staged rollout. Customer confirmed dramatic reduction in failures (98% success during observation window). Follow-ups: deploy to all regions and add fragment-gap alerting to Console dashboards.
